subject: Rates jumped this week. Here's what local homes did.
preheader: Mortgage rates rose to 6.95%, the Fed raised its rate, and August home prices held steady in Sacramento, Placer, and El Dorado counties.
headline: Rates jumped. Local prices held steady.
intro: The average 30-year mortgage rate rose to 6.95% this week, one day after the Federal Reserve raised its own rate.
Here at home, August prices barely moved from a year ago in all three counties, and homes took about a month to sell.
Below is what each number means in plain language, and where to read more.

rates.meaning: A higher rate means a higher monthly payment on the same loan. On a $400,000 loan, the move from 6.76% to 6.95% adds about $50 a month (principal and interest only). Your own rate depends on your credit, down payment, and loan type.

local.attribution: Local numbers: CALIFORNIA ASSOCIATION OF REALTORS® August 2026 home sales and price report, published September 16, 2026. Existing single-family homes, August 1 to 31, 2026, compared with July 2026 and August 2025. Deemed reliable but not guaranteed.

counties.name: Sacramento County
counties.takeaway: Prices are almost exactly where they were a year ago. Homes are selling a few days faster than last August.

counties.name: Placer County
counties.takeaway: Prices are up a little from last year. There are more homes to choose from than in July, and they are taking about a month to sell.

counties.name: El Dorado County
counties.takeaway: The median dropped from July, but it is still above last August. Fewer homes sell here each month, so one month can swing the number a lot. Buyers have the most choices of the three counties.

median_price.meaning: Half sold for more, half for less. A smaller county, so the monthly number jumps around more.

links.title: The Fed raised its interest rate by a quarter point
links.take: The Fed moved its target range up to 3.75% to 4%. The Fed does not set mortgage rates. But its moves change what it costs banks to borrow, and mortgage rates often react.

links.title: California home sales and prices for August
links.take: Statewide, the median price was $901,420, almost flat from a year ago, and the typical home sold in 28 days. Their page has a county table near the bottom, so you can see how our three counties compare with the rest of the state.

links.title: U.S. home sales dipped 2% in August
links.take: Across the country, sales slowed a little and the median price was $429,100. There were 4.9 months of homes for sale, up from 4.6 a year ago, so buyers nationwide have a bit more to pick from.

tip.title: Pre-approved is not the same as pre-qualified
tip.text: Pre-qualified means a lender took a quick look at what you told them. Pre-approved means they checked your pay stubs, credit, and bank statements. When rates are moving, a real pre-approval tells you what payment you can count on before you fall for a house.
